faq.a1: Session Sniffer is 100% external — it passively reads network packets through standard capture drivers (Npcap / libpcap / BPF) and never injects into or modifies game files or memory. There is zero risk of an anti-cheat ban, and all source code is publicly auditable on GitHub under GPLv3.
faq.a2_help: Encountered an issue or have a question? Report bugs on GitHub Issues or ask the community on our Discord Server.
faq.a2_s1: Download the latest Session_Sniffer.exe for Windows (or the Linux / macOS standalone binary from the Download section above).
faq.a2_s3: If prompted on Windows, install Npcap — it is required for network packet capture. On Linux, install libpcap and grant capture capabilities (cap_net_raw); on macOS, grant /dev/bpf* read permissions as shown in the Installation Guide.
faq.a2_s4: Select the network interface you want to sniff from and click Start Sniffing.
faq.a3_s1_eth: Ethernet Cable: Connect an Ethernet cable between your PC and the console and share your PC's internet connection (see the video tutorial below).
faq.a3_s1_title: Share your PC internet connection with the console
faq.a3_s1_wifi: Wi-Fi Hotspot: Use Session Sniffer's built-in Hotspot & Connection Sharing (Capture → Hotspot & Sharing) or Windows Settings "Mobile hotspot" to share your PC's internet connection wirelessly.
faq.a3_s2_desc: Disconnect your PlayStation or Xbox from its current internet connection, then connect it to the Wi-Fi hotspot or Ethernet connection you just shared from your PC.
faq.a3_s2_title: Connect the console to the shared network
faq.a3_s3_desc: Open Session Sniffer and, in the Capture Network Interface Selection window, look for an entry labeled Neighbour in the Type column. Check the Vendor Name column (Microsoft Corporation for Xbox, or Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. for PlayStation) — or cross-reference the IP Address and MAC Address with your console's network settings — then click Start Sniffing.
faq.a3_s3_title: Launch Session Sniffer and select the Neighbour interface
faq.a5: Yes — 100% free and open source under the GNU GPLv3 license, with no paywalls, subscriptions, or telemetry. If you enjoy using it and want to support ongoing development, you can optionally tip on Ko-fi.
faq.a_antivirus_1: Yes — Session Sniffer is safe to run. Some antivirus software flags standalone executables as malware because they are compiled from Python using PyInstaller, which frequently triggers generic false-positive detections even on harmless apps.
faq.a_antivirus_2: The entire source code is open-source and publicly available on GitHub. If you are familiar with Python, you can also run Session Sniffer directly from source, which usually avoids antivirus detections.
faq.a_antivirus_3: In addition, release builds are compiled automatically via GitHub Actions and uploaded by the GitHub Actions bot, so you can review both the build workflow and every build run publicly.
faq.a_arp_s1_desc: From the toolbar, go to Capture → Change Interface — or open Settings → General, disable Auto Connect, and restart Session Sniffer.
faq.a_arp_s1_title: Open the Capture Network Interface Selection screen
faq.a_arp_s2_desc: Check Enable ARP Spoofing in the bottom-right corner of the window.
faq.a_arp_s3_desc: Click Refresh ARP Table in the bottom-left corner of the window. This wakes up devices on your local network so Session Sniffer can identify PlayStation, Xbox, smartphones, and other LAN devices.
faq.a_arp_s4_desc: Select the PlayStation, Xbox, smartphone, or other local device you want to monitor, then click Start Sniffing.
faq.a_arp_s4_title: Choose your device and start sniffing
faq.a_filesize_1: Session Sniffer bundles Python and all required Python dependencies into a single standalone executable so the app works out of the box without requiring you to install anything manually.
faq.a_filesize_2: That self-contained bundle includes the libraries needed for packet scanning, the PySide6 GUI, data handling, themes, translations, and other internal features — which is the main reason the executable file size is relatively large.

features.f1_desc: Operates strictly at the packet layer via Npcap, libpcap, or macOS BPF. Zero memory injection, zero mods required, and zero risk of game bans.
features.f2_desc: Lock capture onto a specific PC game process, or monitor PlayStation, Xbox, and mobile devices via Ethernet sharing, built-in Wi-Fi Hotspot, or LAN ARP.
features.f3_desc: Automatically hides Rockstar, cloud, relay, and game servers so only real players surface — plus custom IP blocklists, ISP filters, and protocol filters.
features.f4_desc: Tag friends or hostiles in UserIP databases with custom names, colors, and notes. Get instant visual popups, TTS voice alerts, and automated detection rules.
features.f5_desc: Real-time Session Host & relay detection, Host History, one-click Solo Public Session, in-game Player Resolver, and Looky System cloud lookups.
features.f6_desc: Inspect live PPS/BPS traffic charts, capture latency graphs, port heatmaps, session timelines, and receive immediate spike alerts on traffic floods.
features.lead: Engineered in Python & PySide6 with native libpcap/Npcap bindings — fast enough for chaotic 30-player sessions without touching game memory.

history.era1_summary: Where Session Sniffer began: built originally as a personal defense against mod-menu crashers, DDoSers, and IP booters on PlayStation 3 across GTA V, GTA IV, Red Dead Redemption, Minecraft, and Call of Duty. This Windows Batch script used TShark to watch live network traffic for blacklisted PSN usernames, triggering instant Windows & webMAN MOD PS3 alerts so you could leave before getting crashed or booted.
history.era2_caption: GTA V Session Sniffer v1.0.0 — First Python TUI Release (Jan 10, 2023)
history.era2_h1: First full Python TUI engine showing all connected & disconnected session peers
history.era2_h2: Early MaxMind GeoLite2 country resolution & per-peer port tracking
history.era2_h3: Worked on PC, Xbox One, and PlayStation without modifying game files
history.era2_summary: Launched on January 10, 2023 alongside PC Blacklist Sniffer, this first Python rewrite happened thanks to my legendary friend {grub4k}, who kindly taught me Python in our free time so I could move on from the slowness and clunkiness of Batch to a much faster language. After having a script that only warned about specific usernames and IPs met in-game, I wanted to display the whole session in my GTA V lobbies — simply because it would be cool, for monitoring and curiosity, and to kill dead time while AFKing in-game and coding. GTA V Session Sniffer v1.0 tracked every connected and disconnected peer in real time with First/Last Seen timestamps, packet counters, ports, and MaxMind GeoLite2 country lookups — without game mods.
history.era2_title: PC Blacklist & GTA V Session Sniffer v1.0
history.era3_caption: GTA V Session Sniffer v1.1.8 — PrettyTable TUI & Host Crown (Nov 6, 2024)
history.era3_h1: Automatic MaxMind GeoLite2 updater & 1,500 IPs/min batch IP-API enrichment
history.era3_h2: LAN ARP scanning, Mobile / VPN / Hosting flags & Session Host crown
history.era3_h3: Sortable PrettyTable TUI, Rejoins / PPS metrics & Discord Rich Presence
history.era3_summary: 2024 was when I truly fell in love with working on and improving this project — coding it literally became fun and a joy to build. That momentum transformed the script into a full intelligence terminal: automatic GeoLite2 database downloads, LAN ARP scanning, 1,500 IPs/min batch IP-API lookups, PrettyTable color-coded connected/disconnected views, Rejoins & PPS metrics, Mobile/VPN/Hosting detection, Session Host crown tracking, and Discord Rich Presence all arrived.
history.era4_caption: Session Sniffer v1.3.0 — First PyQt6 Desktop GUI (Dec 2024 / Jan 2025)
history.era4_h1: First native PyQt6 + QDarkStyle GUI with sortable tables & right-click menus
history.era4_h2: Renamed to universal "Session Sniffer" with standalone Windows .exe builds
history.era4_h3: ICMP/TCP Ping, collapsible tables, Bandwidth stats, TTS alerts & Rich logs
history.era4_summary: The arrival of AI is what immediately pushed me to opt for a Python GUI — and I'm not ashamed to admit it. Sticking with Python was an easy call: the entire source code and backend were already built and rock-solid, and all I needed was a graphical interface on top. On December 15, 2024, the terminal evolved into a native PyQt6 desktop app, and on January 4, 2025 the project dropped "GTA V" to become universal Session Sniffer — adding standalone .exe builds, right-click context menus, ICMP/TCP/spoofed Ping, Wireshark MAC lookups, collapsible tables, bandwidth metrics, TTS voice alerts, and ARP spoofing.
history.era5_caption: Session Sniffer v1.5.0 — Modern Cross-Platform PySide6 Suite (Nov 2026)
history.era5_h1: PySide6 UI + native libpcap/Npcap/BPF engine (no TShark required) on Windows, Linux & macOS
history.era5_h2: RDR2 feature set, Looky System, Live Graphs, Port Scanner, Hotspot & LAN Web Dashboard
history.era5_h3: 6 built-in themes + 20-color Theme Manager & 33 languages with full RTL layout
history.era5_summary: The largest overhaul in the project's history — and still proudly built in Python. Even with AI, I never wanted to build a sniffer in another language I don't know: I know Python, so I code in Python, I refuse to be blind to the code AI generates, and I want fine control to stay completely in charge — that's what modern-day programming is now, at least for me. Re-architected into a modular PySide6 suite with native libpcap/Npcap/BPF capture (eliminating TShark) across Windows, Linux, and macOS, it added RDR2 tools, Looky System, Live Graphs, Detections & Combo Rules, Embedded LAN Web Panel with QR Code, Wi-Fi Hotspot Manager, 6 themes + Theme Manager, and 33 languages with RTL.

history.v_1_0_0: Initial Python TUI release of GTA V Session Sniffer tracking connected & disconnected peers, First/Last Seen timestamps, packet counters, ports, and country lookup.

history.v_1_1_0: Added automatic MaxMind GeoLite2 database downloads & updates, LAN ARP scanning, and customizable field sorting & PPS timers.
history.v_1_1_6: Added Mobile, VPN/Proxy, and Hosting detection columns, Rejoins counter, 1,500 IPs/min batch IP-API lookups, and Session Host crown detection (v1.1.6 – v1.1.9).
history.v_1_2_0: Refined PrettyTable TUI tables, added Discord Rich Presence, and expanded verified compatibility across PC, PS3, PS5, and Xbox One (v1.2.0 – v1.2.9).
history.v_1_3_0: Landmark PyQt6 + QDarkStyle desktop GUI rewrite and official rename to "Session Sniffer", adding right-click context menus, UserIP colors, and multi-cell selection/copy.
history.v_1_3_3: Shipped standalone PyInstaller .exe builds with bundled TShark/Npcap, ICMP/TCP/spoofed Ping actions, Pinging column, and accelerated reverse-DNS resolution (v1.3.3 – v1.3.6).
history.v_1_3_7: Adopted PEP 440 UTC build-timestamp versioning, improved capture interface discovery, and fixed broadcast/multicast filtering (v1.3.7 – v1.3.7post6).
history.v_1_3_8: Switched MAC vendor lookup to the Wireshark manuf database, improved global PPS calculations, and added toolbar quick-links (v1.3.8 – v1.3.8.post2).
history.v_1_3_9: Introduced live detection warnings for Mobile, VPN, and Hosting connections alongside GUI notification toggle controls.
history.v_1_4_0: Added collapsible Connected/Disconnected tables with live player counts, improved minimized-table performance, and hardened Session Host IP handling.
history.v_1_4_1: Major core code reorganization splitting monolithic capture, lookup, and rendering logic into cleaner modules.
history.v_1_4_2: Improved ARP spoofing error diagnostics, strict IP/port validation, consolidated exceptions, and stabilized TShark capture lifecycles (v1.4.2 – v1.4.2.post5).
history.v_1_4_3: Added Bandwidth metrics, hideable packet columns, modular GUI color system, Jane/Liam TTS voice notifications, and Rich structured logging (v1.4.3 – v1.4.3.post4).
history.v_1_5_0: 2,100+ commits & 115 release candidates: modular src/ package, PySide6 UI, native libpcap/Npcap/BPF capture (no TShark), Windows/Linux/macOS binaries, RDR2 toolkit, Looky System, Live Graphs, Combo Rules, LAN Web Panel + QR Code, Hotspot Manager, Port Scanner, 6 Themes + Theme Manager, and 33 languages with RTL.
